methodology:
SLC Agrícola operates 26 production units across 8 Brazilian states. The original 16-unit portfolio expanded with several recent acquisitions (Pamplona, Pioneira JV with Dois Vales, expanded Parnaguá +14,572 ha in 2024). Properties named below are confirmed via SLC IR materials with hectares from 2018-2024 disclosures.

Production unit naming convention: each SLC unit name starts with "P" and has 8 letters (Pamplona, Pioneira, Paiaguás, Palmares, Parnaíba, Planeste, Planorte, Parceiro, Parnaguá, Panorama, Piratini, Paladino, etc.) — a notable corporate idiosyncrasy.

The 12 named units shown total ~937K acres / ~379K hectares — about 54% of SLC's total ~700K hectare owned base. Smaller units (Paladino, Parnaíba II, Planalto, etc.) aggregated in the final row totaling ~793K acres.

Per-acre FMVs reflect 2024-2025 IMEA, AGEFAZ, and regional broker data:
- Western Bahia (LEM): R$8,500-10,000/acre — Palmares, Parceiro
- Goiás Class-A: R$7,500-9,000/acre — Pamplona
- Mato Grosso Class-A: R$6,500-8,500/acre — Paiaguás, Planorte, Panorama
- MS Class-A: R$6,500-7,500/acre — Piratini  
- Matopiba (MA/PI/TO): R$5,500-7,500/acre — Planeste, Parnaíba, Pioneira, Parnaguá

Total FMV ~R$11.4B vs. ~R$4.5B GAAP cost-basis book reflects Brazilian GAAP accounting + SLC's own internally-disclosed R$15B land bank value at capital markets day 2024.

Data caveats:
- Hectares for Panorama / Piratini are estimates (LandCo subsidiary properties less granularly disclosed)
- "Other named units" aggregate covers ~14 smaller farms; refining individual hectares would tighten the per-region distribution
